# Remaining confirmed-element thermal reviews — 5 October 2026

This stage completes the requested remaining **0035–0118 source-accession sweep**, using the existing [selector](../../data/research/mat-update-review.json), [MAT-TODO](../../data/quality/MAT-TODO.json) and [handoff](../../MAT_CODEX_CONTINUATION_HANDOFF.md). It does not complete every scientific domain or image. MAT-PROGRAMME-DATA-FIRST remains PARTIAL. Origin/Hydrogen identities and all previous authored science remain canonical.

## Implemented and improved

All 84 remaining records now have a source-bound supplement or explicit review. Seventeen verified pages supply 56 published Shomate fits, 5,656 calculated rows, linked CSV/Markdown tables and 17 phase-specific SVG charts. Fifty-nine identity-verified pages lack a Shomate table in the retained response. Eight exact-name queries for 0111–0118 return Name Not Found; their retained responses are lookup evidence, not elemental measurements. Returned formula, CAS and molar basis are UNKNOWN. In these 67 new gaps, heat capacity stays null and uncertainty UNKNOWN; zero fit counts are not physical zeros.

Bromine and Iodine retain **mol Br2** and **mol I2**, each containing two atoms per formula. Strict formula parsing rejects compounds, charged/mismatched species and invalid counts; no factor-of-two change to their published coefficients is made. Neutral Tellurium and Polonium were selected from actual source links; charged Te and molecular Po2 candidates were not substituted. Each source phase and fit interval remains separate; no equilibrium dissociation, phase stability, transport property, pressure dependence or missing covariance is inferred.

The [dated JANAF index](https://janaf.nist.gov/janaf4pdf.html), SRC-000341, retains its 29 September date and exact bytes. Actual linked/unlinked cells are preserved; a linked element-organised PDF requires a separate elemental-species/phase review and does not automatically supply accepted Cp data. Source IDs SRC-000424–SRC-000507 were allocated after reserving existing and unresolved historical identities. The [original intake ledger](../../data/intake/user-reference-batches-2026-09-14.json) retains the reserved unresolved identifier shown below. This is a historical identifier reservation, not a citation supporting physical data; its source remains unregistered.

```text
SRC-000423
```

No historical reference was silently reassigned.

The bounded gap contract distinguishes an identity-checked no-fit page, a retained no-match response and an unretrieved lookup. A requested formula is not a returned identity; a review date is not a retrieval date. Changed marker-bearing gap owners are now protected against silent overwrite. Legacy and physical asset-slot collision checks protect authored curated records.

## Publisher arithmetic and evidence limits

All 538 new publisher rows are checked with their own printed decimal precision. Bromine prints its first temperature as 333. K while its fit begins at 332.503 K. The latter is inside the printed cell's 332.5–333.5 K formatting interval and is the only retained fit endpoint there that matches all three rounded Cp/entropy/enthalpy cells. The exact underlying publisher temperature remains unconfirmed. Both nominal/raw and source-boundary calculation temperatures are retained. The endpoint is used only after nominal comparison failure, with independent endpoint/format-cell/quantity checks; no tolerance is widened. This is formatting interpretation, not physical uncertainty. All other new comparison rows agree at their printed temperatures.

New fits pass 101 positive/finite samples each. Unknown coefficient uncertainty/covariance remains UNKNOWN; generated values are CALCULATED-FROM-PUBLISHED-FIT, not measured. Transcription, numerical identities, source hashes and software tests do not independently replicate experiments or certify an element complete. Actual terminal tests, build, browser, preservation and copy results are retained in the [batch receipt](../../data/quality/thermal-remaining-elements-batch-2026-10-05.json) and handoff.
